why: Replaces the coined term 'governor' with the plain word 'question'.
Shorter; the added demo bullet is a low-value extra sentence.
Names the actor ('The LLM') and gives concrete failure modes with a hedge ('may') instead of a flat claim.
Tells the student they don't need to build these today and can ask the agent; B is a clever 'all cost less' overclaim.
'Guardrails' is plain; 'rails' is a coined term the author cuts.
Cuts the extra forward-pointing sentence.
Shorter, and 'grounded in quoted moments' is looser and easier to read.
Drops the 'on the map' sentence, which is about the course structure.
Plain and short; B's 'send the work back for correction' is wordier.
Shorter and clearer ending; A's last line is a clever kicker.
Gives a concrete reason and permission for the time budget; A's 'buys the clues' is vaguer.
Concrete mechanism in plain words; A's 'Today the file exists' is a vague kicker.
Drops the 'decision only you can make' flourish for a plain claim; reorders to lead with the point.
Replaces the 'identity' aside and the 'matters more than it sounds' filler with one plain fact.
B adds the kicker 'artifact, not a feeling' after the point was already made.
A is shorter and its steering section closes the point in few words; B adds a bulky restating section.
Cuts the bolded slogan 'Never let the agent say everything'.
Names the actor ('The LLM') instead of 'It'; the two versions are otherwise identical.
'Infinite chameleon' is a coined metaphor that A leans on; B uses the plain 'mirror'.
B narrates what the student just did and adds an off-topic aside; A states the action.
A ends on a dangling heading and a third bullet; B is shorter and stays on the topic.
Fewer sentences; B adds an italic rhetorical question and an 'agent finds, you judge' restatement.
Header B names what the student did; A's header is a vague line that describes nothing.
Cuts the slide about how the course was built.
Shorter; B adds forward-pointing explanation and a redundant 'diagnostic' sentence.
Cuts a redundant lead-in sentence fragment; same point in fewer words.
B adds a whole optional exercise and a long recap; A is the compact narration, and shorter wins.
Cuts 'Worth a moment of looking', a low-value closer.
'Module 4's send-off' is concrete; B's parenthetical about the module file is about the course's structure.
'The choice is yours' is a redundant closer after 'Pick the shape'.
'Compounded the run' is shorter and uses the training's own word; A's header is wordy.
Drops the 'task is the assay' item, a coined extra metaphor; fewer words.
'Container' is more literal than 'a place to hang moves', which repeats the hanging metaphor.
Plain statement; B's 'cargo/vehicle' metaphor is an invented clever line.
B's bare 'At least 10% wrong' is ungrammatical, loses the 'Remember' frame, and adds an unrelated Homework block.
Much shorter; B's 'Why for Module 3' repeats and its source caveat is course-internal meta.
The permission line is a narrator's reassurance and adds no information; shorter wins.
A's 'Why for Module 5' lines are plain and consistent. B adds sentences and a framing paragraph, and it swaps 'quicksilver' for 'mercury-like'.
B's added clause ('on the hook', 'You read what lands') is filler. A is the shorter version.
The forward hint to the next lecture is low value, so cut it.
B drops the 'You ask; the agent drafts' narration and gives a clearer instruction. It's shorter and opens on the action.
The closer 'The exercise teaches the move. You take the move home.' is a clever line after the point, so cut it.
B's 'Execution is next module's concern' is a forward hint. B's ask is also more convoluted. A is shorter and clear.
B is shorter and cuts the extra instruction, though the clause in A that tells Claude to check auto-load has some value. Shorter wins by default.
The clause defining the primitive ('an automated check that says this meets the bar') makes the concept concrete for readers who don't know it.
'Hand off to the ticket close.' is a course-navigation line. Cut it.
'Decide' puts the student in control. 'Steer' is fine, but B is the stronger verb for who controls the LLM.
The title in B restates the point the body makes. A's shorter title is enough.
Shorter; B's 'every module after this one' is a forward hint.
Cuts the clever kicker callout and the vague closer; adds a concrete file location.
Cuts the closing sentence that adds little.
Removes the low-value explanatory sentence; shorter.
B's 'Before you ran it, that was a name' congratulates and narrates what the student felt.
B's added sentence restates what the next bullet says.
B adds a bullet about automation shapes, which is a forward hint and not hands-on.
B swaps in a clever slogan closer; A's line is human and plain.
Plain, student-controlled instruction and no 'stiffer' put-down.
'Came out of one ticket' is plainer than 'the ticket gave up two things'.
B adds a course-internal M5 terminology aside that costs words.
'The agent forgets' is a concrete reason and 'goal drifts' is vaguer; B names the actor.
'Judging' matches the 'find vs judge' frame of the slide; 'checking' is vaguer and less precise.
A states the principle first, then the example, then the move; B has the wrong order and adds a course-about-itself closer plus a second slide.
Same content in fewer words; drops the explanatory tail about untracked fills.
Cuts a narrator sentence ('You stop seeing every move…') that restates the point; fewer sentences per slide.
Shorter, though 'toy game' is loaded; A's extra sentence about Module 3 and STRIDE is a forward hint, so B wins.
Cuts the forward pointer to Module 3 about what the slide will cover later.
Cuts a recap sentence that only restates the arc; shorter.
B adds a trainer-about-the-slide sentence ('This one runs on the screen. Watch…') and a vaguer closer; A is tighter.
The added claim that nothing edits source until approval is true and useful, and it stays in the same bullet.
The bullet only restates the prompt's purpose; shorter wins when a whole low-value sentence goes.
'Writes a plan' is plainer than 'drafts the steps'; both versions are the same length, and A is more literal.
The clause on the other two options makes the instruction concrete and true; it is a condition worth keeping.
Cuts the course-about-itself title line and the 'Not X but' rhetorical contrast; shorter, neutral.
Drops the redundant slogan opener; the list already says it.
Cuts the filler 'We have come a long way' sentence.
Drops the 'You are here' slide about the course map and where the training goes next.
